body_markdown:
While the featured builds draw the most attention each year at SEMA, we still get excited to see what innovations the industry has cooked up. We found a host of interesting products for finishing up a restoration, finding extra horsepower, and simplifying an engine swap. Check out some of the ones that caught our eye below.


## Trick Flow Shaft-Mounted Rockers for Mopar Big-Blocks


[Brandan Gillogly](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/brandan-gillogly/)


MSRP: TBA


Trick Flow might have made a name for itself with its small-block Ford performance parts, but it also manufactures Chevy and Mopar parts, and its Power Port line of CNC-ported Mopar cylinder heads, in particular, has been taking off lately. The brand’s newest offering is shaft-mounted rockers for the big Mopar V-8 that are a perfect match for those heads. Spintron-tested for durability, the rockers are available in 1.5:1 and 1.6:1 ratios.


## BTR SBC Accessory Drive


[Brandan Gillogly](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/brandan-gillogly/)


MSRP: $2299.99


Brian Tooley Racing specializes in late-model performance for LS/LT GM V-8s, Gen III Hemis, and Ford’s Godzilla V-8s, but this drive kit goes in a different direction. Coy Hudnall from BTR gave us the lowdown on one of the first parts BTR has made for Gen I small-block Chevys. Its new front accessory drive system is based on a proprietary water pump manifold that mounts all of the other accessories. “We pull this whole thing forward just a little bit further than you would see a normal factory accessory drive,” Coy explained. That allows the alternator, power steering pump, and A/C compressor—all late-model parts— to move just in front of the cylinder heads. “So everything’s pulled in tight,” Coy said, “about as tight as you can get it.” Everything bolts to the water pump manifold, which uses a serviceable cartridge. BTR includes the wiring and plumbing adapters needed, and aside from the crank pulley, which installs last, almost the whole assembly can be put together on a bench and installed on an engine in one go. We’re always glad to see innovative products for one of hot-rodders’ favorite engines, but we’re also excited to see more small-block parts from BTR.


## Procharger High Output Tuner Kit for 1988–96 F-150/Bronco


[Brandan Gillogly](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/brandan-gillogly/)


MSRP: $5338


We have a soft spot for the[first-gen Ford Lightning](https://www.hagerty.com/media/market-trends/fords-first-gen-f150-lightning-has-taken-off-as-a-modern-collector-truck/) . They look great and came with a solid 351 Windsor V-8. The downside is that they got blown out of the water by their supercharged Modular V-8 successor. Procharger’s new supercharger kit includes a D-1SC supercharger with a self-contained oiling system that can support 650 horsepower and more than level the playing field. Options include helical gears for less noise, charge coolers, and a black or polished finish. Builders will have to provide the engine with enough fuel and sort out tuning on their own, and so far there’s no CARB EO number for California emissions.


## FAST XCR LS3 Intake


[Brandan Gillogly](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/brandan-gillogly/)


MSRP: TBA


The factory intake manifolds that come on GM’s Gen III and Gen IV engines aren’t bad, but FAST has found a few ways to improve on them. The brand’s latest intake has moved the fuel injectors and fuel rails inside the plenum to package longer, straighter runners than would normally be possible. Think of it like a cross ram with the simplicity of a single throttle body. The result is improved cylinder filling and improved power from 2500-7000 rpm, with gains of 30-40 hp over factory intakes. FAST is offering the design for rectangular-port, LS3-style cylinder heads in two versions: one for 102/103mm throttle bodies and another built for 112mm throttle bodies.


## Milodon Gen III Hemi Engine Swap Oil Pan


[Brandan Gillogly](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/brandan-gillogly/)


MSRP: $505


This one isn’t exactly new, but it was new to us. Milodon offers engine swap oil pans for all kinds of cars, with a lot of applications that help swap Gen III Hemi V-8s into classic Mopar metal. The one we photographed above is for 1965-1974 A, B, and E bodies. Not only does it fit the factory K-member with room to spare, but the windage tray keeps oil where it’s supposed to be and will actually net a few horsepower over the factory piece. If your Slant Six or 318 is a bit worn out and a junkyard 5.7L Hemi would scratch your horsepower itch, Milodon might have what you need to make the swap easier.


## Classic Instruments 1970–74 Challenger Dash Panel and Gauges


[Brandan Gillogly](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/brandan-gillogly/)


MSRP: $2055


Now that they’re more than 50 years old, the interior plastics on the average first-gen Dodge Challenger are likely one harsh glance away from cracking, assuming they haven’t already. Classic Instruments now offers a complete ABS plastic dash panel set with the appropriate gauges and sending units to restore the look of Dodge’s original ponycar. Available in black, carbon fiber, and brushed aluminum with your choice of gauge finish, these dashes are made in the U.S.
